_doc: Named example stores (fictional names, real-ish UK contexts). Each points to a format config + planogram in data/store/formats/. Every number has a source or 'assumption:'. Built by scripts/scale_superstore.py.

stores.name: Ludgate Lane Express
stores.context: express · office district (City fringe, weekday lunch trade)

customers_per_week.source: data/ops/params.json store_customers_per_week range low end: Gruen & Corsten (2008) 'smaller format' 4,000 customers/week (US illustrative; medium confidence)

footfall_curve.hour_multipliers_source: assumption: office district: lunch (meal deal) and commute peaks; the NTS commute peak at 17:00 (params commute_trip_start_share_17h) anchors the evening bump
footfall_curve.day_multipliers_source: assumption: offices shut at weekends; weekday NTS day shares otherwise
footfall_curve.formula: arrivals/h = customers_per_week x day_share x hour_share x hour_multiplier x day_multiplier, renormalised so the week sums to customers_per_week

mission_mix_source.baseline_source: derived: params mission_mix_by_daypart (assumption, low confidence) weighted by the NTS hour shares of each daypart window 08-22
mission_mix_source.multipliers_source: assumption: an office-district express is a meal-deal + top-up store; almost no weekly shops
mission_mix_source.note: 'treat' covers the family after-school trip (params 15-17 window); missions use the params keys so the ops engine can consume them

persona_weights_source.rule: derived: weight(persona) = mission_mix[persona.mission] / (number of personas with that mission) x multiplier, renormalised. persona.mission from data/personas/lens/<archetype>.json
persona_weights_source.multipliers_source: assumption: office workers are habit-led at lunch; fewer parents shopping for kids; GLP-1 users buy small portions at lunch

customers_per_week.source: data/ops/params.json store_customers_per_week range low end (Gruen & Corsten 2008 smaller format)

footfall_curve.hour_multipliers_source: assumption: students shop late; lunch peak between lectures
footfall_curve.formula: arrivals/h = customers_per_week x day_share x hour_share x hour_multiplier x day_multiplier, renormalised so the week sums to customers_per_week

mission_mix_source.baseline_source: derived: params mission_mix_by_daypart (assumption, low confidence) weighted by the NTS hour shares of each daypart window 08-22
mission_mix_source.multipliers_source: assumption: students buy meal deals, top-ups, treats and gym food; few big shops in an express
mission_mix_source.note: 'treat' covers the family after-school trip (params 15-17 window); missions use the params keys so the ops engine can consume them

persona_weights_source.rule: derived: weight(persona) = mission_mix[persona.mission] / (number of personas with that mission) x multiplier, renormalised. persona.mission from data/personas/lens/<archetype>.json
persona_weights_source.multipliers_source: assumption: student budgets (frugal), TikTok-driven trial, higher vegan share; few parents; fewer habit loyalists

customers_per_week.source: data/ops/params.json store_customers_per_week: Gruen & Corsten (2008) supermarket cost example, 10,900 customers/week (US illustrative; medium confidence)

footfall_curve.hour_multipliers_source: assumption: high-street lunch and after-work bumps on top of the NTS curve
footfall_curve.formula: arrivals/h = customers_per_week x day_share x hour_share x hour_multiplier x day_multiplier, renormalised so the week sums to customers_per_week

mission_mix_source.baseline_source: derived: params mission_mix_by_daypart (assumption, low confidence) weighted by the NTS hour shares of each daypart window 08-22
mission_mix_source.multipliers_source: assumption: high-street metro skews to top-up and lunch vs the params baseline
mission_mix_source.note: 'treat' covers the family after-school trip (params 15-17 window); missions use the params keys so the ops engine can consume them

persona_weights_source.rule: derived: weight(persona) = mission_mix[persona.mission] / (number of personas with that mission) x multiplier, renormalised. persona.mission from data/personas/lens/<archetype>.json
persona_weights_source.multipliers_source: no adjustment: params baseline mission mix carries the persona split

stores.name: Kingsmead Superstore
stores.context: superstore · retail park (car-borne family big shop)

customers_per_week.source: assumption: ~2x the Gruen & Corsten (2008) 10,900/week supermarket example for a large retail-park superstore; no UK store-level footfall source fetched (data/ops/evidence.md gaps)

footfall_curve.hour_multipliers_source: assumption: after-school family trips (NTS escort-education peak 15:00, params school_escort_trip_start_share_15h)
footfall_curve.day_multipliers_source: assumption: retail-park Saturday skew on top of the NTS Saturday share (1.45x average day)
footfall_curve.formula: arrivals/h = customers_per_week x day_share x hour_share x hour_multiplier x day_multiplier, renormalised so the week sums to customers_per_week

mission_mix_source.baseline_source: derived: params mission_mix_by_daypart (assumption, low confidence) weighted by the NTS hour shares of each daypart window 08-22
mission_mix_source.multipliers_source: assumption: car-borne big shop; 'treat' includes the family after-school trip (params after_school_treat_uplift)
mission_mix_source.note: 'treat' covers the family after-school trip (params 15-17 window); missions use the params keys so the ops engine can consume them

persona_weights_source.rule: derived: weight(persona) = mission_mix[persona.mission] / (number of personas with that mission) x multiplier, renormalised. persona.mission from data/personas/lens/<archetype>.json
persona_weights_source.multipliers_source: assumption: families with children dominate retail-park big shops; value-seeking on big baskets
